prompt_scale.note: Common-suite prompts are tiny. C1 'prefill' rows measure fixed per-request serving cost, not bulk prefill throughput. GPU floor for one ~45-token prompt is ~one weight sweep (~66 ms at 256 GB/s over 17.1 GB).

per_request_fixed_cost_ms.source: sweep wall_seconds x 10 requests (complete-wall protocol); llama.cpp internal prompt_ms is 257-320 of each ~300-357 ms wall at the winner cluster.

p12_engine_delta_attribution.verdict: Every fork delta that is active on standard Q4_K_M is Vulkan cooperative-matrix matmul tuning (LDS padding/bank conflicts/wave32/f16 operands) plus GDN concat-transpose tiling - i.e. Vulkan catching up to the HIP backend. Stock HIP reaches the prefill winner cluster without any fork change (C1-C8: 136.8/172.0/180.1/192.5/217.4/241.1/242.1/274.1 vs winners 139.0/194.1/180.1/192.5/217.4/243.5/245.6/296.8; within 1.6-12.8% per cell).
p12_engine_delta_attribution.port_implication: No fork kernel port is required for hipEngine (HIP-native) prefill parity. The prefill gap is hipEngine's per-request serving cost (628 ms vs ~323-332 ms winner cluster), consistent with the P1.3 hypothesis. Fork port candidates remain parked for P2.3 only if a below-serving-boundary wall is later proven.
p12_engine_delta_attribution.mtp_note: At C1, fork MTP (21.0-21.3) matches current mainline (21.0); the older stock-HIP pin lags (17.6) but wins C8 (54.8). MTP deltas between rows are small relative to hipEngine's 3.0x gap; the E-phase campaign remains the MTP vehicle.
p12_engine_delta_attribution.bisect_decision: Full rebuild bisect of both forks declined as not evidence-bearing for this campaign: identical flags + stock-HIP control already separate config from code, and no active-on-Q4_K_M fork change is a hipEngine port candidate.
